chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Abu Shu'ayb al-Mahamili al-Rifa'i, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who hired another man to dig a well to a depth of ten qamat (statures) for ten dirhams. He dug one qama, then was unable to dig further. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'For him is one part out of fifty-five parts from the ten dirhams.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu al-Mu'alla, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

He said: Umar ibn al-Khattab was brought a woman who had attached herself to a man from the Ansar and desired him, but could not find a way to him. So she went, took an egg, extracted the yolk, and poured the white onto her clothes between her thighs. Then she came to Umar and said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, this man took me in such and such a place and disgraced me.'

He said: Umar inclined to punish the Ansari, so the Ansari began swearing oaths, while the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was seated, saying, 'O Commander of the Faithful, be firm in my matter.' When the youth had sworn much, Umar said to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), 'O Abu al-Hasan, what do you see?'

So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) looked at the whiteness on the woman's garment between her thighs and suspected that she had devised a trick for that. So he said, 'Bring me hot water that has boiled with intense boiling,' so they did so.

When the water was brought, he ordered them to pour it upon the place of the whiteness, so that whiteness solidified. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) took it and cast it into his mouth. When he recognized its taste, he threw it out from his mouth. Then he turned to the woman until she confessed to that, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, spared the Ansari from Umar's punishment.

key_terms.دَرَاهِمَ: dirhams, silver coins used as currency
key_terms.قَامَاتٍ: statures or cubits, a unit of depth measurement

ai.seo_question: How is partial payment calculated when a worker stops before completing the agreed task, and how did the Imam identify the woman's trick?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical application of *fiqh* in daily transactions and social dynamics, specifically highlighting the principle of proportional compensation (*nisbah*) for partial work completion. The second narrative showcases Imam al-Sadiq’s keen observational skills and judicial wisdom, as he discerns the woman’s stratagem by tasting the egg yolk, thereby protecting the Ansari man from unjust punishment by Umar ibn al-Khattab. These accounts underscore the Shia emphasis on justice, fairness in contracts, and the Imam’s role as a discerning arbiter in resolving disputes.
